name: Dhansak
subtitle: sunday mutton simmered into a purée of four dals and gourds, sour and gently hot

image.alt: Parsi dhansak with caramelised brown rice

ingredients.qty: 700g, shoulder on the bone, cut into 4cm pieces
ingredients.note: bone is what makes the gravy
the backbone of the dal mix
the bitter note that defines dhansak
the sliced one is for the brown onion garnish

prepNotes: Rinse the four dals together and soak them 45 minutes; they cook far more evenly.
Bring the mutton to room temperature 30 minutes ahead so it browns instead of steaming.
Soak the tamarind in hot water while the dals cook, then squeeze and strain out the fibres.

steps.text: Pressure cook the drained dals with the pumpkin, eggplant, methi leaves, chopped onion, tomato, turmeric and 1 litre of water for 5 whistles, about 20 minutes.
steps.tip: The vegetables melt away. That is the point. Do not keep them chunky.

steps.text: Meanwhile heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy pan and brown the mutton in two batches over high heat, 5 minutes a batch.
steps.tip: Crowding the pan is the single most common mistake; the meat will grey instead of crusting.

steps.text: Pound the garlic, ginger and green chilli to a coarse paste and fry it in the same pan for 2 minutes, until the raw smell lifts.
Add the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, black pepper, coriander powder, cumin powder, chilli powder and garam masala and fry 90 seconds, splashing in 2 tbsp water when it catches.
Return the mutton, add 200ml water, cover and simmer 45 minutes until a knife slides into the meat with no resistance.
Cool the dal mixture slightly, fish out any large spice pieces, and blend to a smooth, pourable purée.
steps.tip: Blend it hot and it will spit. Wait ten minutes, and leave the lid vented.

steps.text: Pour the purée over the mutton, add the tamarind extract, jaggery and salt, and simmer uncovered 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes.
steps.tip: It sticks readily once thick. Use a flat wooden spoon and scrape the base.

steps.text: Taste and balance. It should land sour first, then sweet, then hot. Add tamarind or jaggery a teaspoon at a time.
Fry the sliced onion in the remaining 2 tbsp oil until dark brown and crisp, about 10 minutes over medium heat.
Rest the dhansak 10 minutes off the heat, then top with the fried onion, mint and coriander leaves.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and freezes well for 2 months. It thickens overnight. Loosen with hot water and reheat gently, as a fast reheat scorches the dal.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
